The Cleaver

GeometryTriangles
Game: The green line cuts the edge of the triangle into two pieces of the same length. Change the triangle and see that it always does.
How to play: Drag a blue corner, or the inside of the triangle, or focus a corner and use the arrow keys. Tick the boxes to show the names and the steps of the proof.
Look for the math

A line through the midpoint M of side AB, parallel to the bisector of angle C, meets the longer of the other two sides at D. M and D cut the perimeter of the triangle into two equal halves. The line is called a cleaver.

The statement

Take AC longer than BC. CL is the angle bisector at C, M is the midpoint of AB, and MD is parallel to CL with D on AC. Then

AM + AD = BM + BC + CD

Both sides are half the perimeter. The line under the picture adds them up for the triangle on the board.

Why it works

Extend AC past C to F with CF = CB (the "premise" marks). Triangle BCF is isosceles, so the bisector of its angle at C is perpendicular to BF. That bisector is also perpendicular to CL, because the inner and outer bisectors at a corner are at right angles. So CL is parallel to BF, and so is MD. In triangle ABF the line MD runs from the midpoint of AB parallel to BF, so by the midpoint theorem D is the midpoint of AF (the "statement" arrows). Hence AD = DF = CD + BC, and adding AM = BM gives the equation above.

Three cleavers

Every side has a cleaver from its midpoint, and the three meet at one point, the Spieker center. That point is the incenter of the triangle formed by the three midpoints. The logic test checks every step of the proof, and this meeting point, on 5,000 random triangles and on a grid of 2,500 places for C. Each claim held every time.

Drag C until AC and BC are equal. The cleaver slides onto the bisector and D lands on C. Pull C past that point and D jumps to the other side.

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
